samples.summary: logout() erases under a stale identity: the persisted offline-user mirror is refreshed only where OfflineRuntime mounts, so a second account's sign-out can destroy the first account's stored documents and un-pushed work
samples.evidence: `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` takes `who = offlineUserId()`, which falls back to `localStorage['wafflebase-offline-user']` (offline-erase.ts:98-107). That mirror is written in exactly one place — `rememberOfflineUser(userId)` inside `OfflineRuntime`'s effect (offline-runtime.tsx:66) — and `OfflineRuntime` is mounted only when `offlineInPlay` is true (`PrivateRoute.tsx:28-30,58`: `supportsClientKey() || getOfflinePersistenceEnabled(me.id)`). There is no check anywhere that the mirrored id is the account actually signing out. Scenario the change itself anticipates (PrivateRoute.tsx:52-54 mentions "if the pin is later rolled back"): user A opts in on a capable build and stores documents, mirror = "A". The pin is rolled back, so `supportsClientKey()` is false. User B signs in on the same device and has never opted in, so `offlineInPlay` is false for B and `OfflineRuntime` never mounts — the mirror still reads "A". B clicks Log out from the authenticated shell; `logout()` reaches `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` (api/auth.ts:134-136), which resolves `who = "A"`, calls `denyOfflineWrites("A")`, `store.dropAllForUser("A")` and `forgetDeviceSecret("A")` — deleting A's live entries (which carry the un-pushed change log this feature exists to preserve) and A's archives, on a sign-out that was not A's. The same stale id also reaches `purgeOfflineDocuments()` (offline-erase.ts:412) and `isOfflineUser()` (offline-erase.ts:116-118), so a document B deletes in a shared workspace purges A's local copy of it.
searchedFor: Grep rememberOfflineUser across packages/frontend/src (only call site is offline-runtime.tsx:66 plus the internal clears in offline-erase.ts)
Read PrivateRoute.tsx to confirm the offlineInPlay gate around <OfflineRuntime/>
Read api/auth.ts logout() for any identity check before eraseOfflineDataOnLogout

samples.summary: DurableYorkieProvider creates a WafflebaseDocStore but never closes it, leaking an IndexedDB connection for every durable document opened in a session
samples.evidence: The store is built in `useMemo(() => new WafflebaseDocStore({...}), [userId])` at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:148 and there is no cleanup effect that calls `store.close()` — grepping `.close()` across packages/frontend/src returns offline-runtime.tsx:231 and offline-erase.ts (345/377/426/553) only, never this file. `WafflebaseDocStore.open()` memoizes a live `IDBDatabase` handle on first use, so each durable document the user opens and navigates away from leaves an open connection held for the lifetime of the tab. Every other owner of a store in this change closes it in a `finally` or an effect cleanup; this one is the long-lived, per-document one and is the only one that does not.

samples.summary: watchForOfflineDisable's fallback store is created and never closed, leaking a connection on the erase path it exists to serve
samples.evidence: `const current = store() ?? new WafflebaseDocStore({ userId: who });` (offline-erase.ts:612) then `void eraseOfflineData(current, who).catch(...)` (620). When the caller supplies no store — the documented main case, since Settings is a route where no editor is mounted — this freshly constructed instance opens the database and is never closed; unlike `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` (345), `purgeOfflineDocuments` (426) and `retryPendingOfflineErase` (377), there is no `finally { store.close() }`. Each toggle-off leaks one connection.
searchedFor: Compared against the finally { store.close() } in the three sibling functions in the same file

samples.summary: OfflineRuntime's cleanup closes the store while its async housekeeping is still running; the store silently reopens, so a cancelled session's sweep/purge continues against a connection nothing will close
samples.evidence: The cleanup sets `cancelled = true` and calls `store.close()` (offline-runtime.tsx:223-232), but the IIFE started at line 128 only checks `cancelled` *between* steps — it can be inside `store.collectStale()` (146), `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` or a per-item `fetchDocument` when the cleanup runs. `WafflebaseDocStore.close()` merely clears `this.db`/`this.opening` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:533-537), so the very next `await this.open()` inside that in-flight work reopens the database — the deletions continue for a component that has unmounted, and the reopened connection is never closed because the only `close()` call already ran. The user-visible effect is a destructive sweep continuing after the authenticated shell has been torn down (e.g. the user navigated to a share link) plus a dangling handle.
searchedFor: Read offline-runtime.tsx effect body and cleanup
Read WafflebaseDocStore.close()/open() to confirm the reopen-on-next-use behaviour

samples.summary: rememberOfflineUser lifts the post-erase write denial before the owed erase is retried, and leaves it lifted permanently if the retry fails again
samples.evidence: `rememberOfflineUser(userId)` calls `permitOfflineWrites(userId)` unconditionally (offline-erase.ts:77-82). `OfflineRuntime` calls it at line 66 of offline-runtime.tsx, *before* `await retryPendingOfflineErase()` at line 134. So for an account whose sign-out erase failed — the exact case `denyOfflineWrites` documents as "It stands even if the erase below fails" (offline-erase.ts:327-329) — signing back in re-permits writes while the erase is still owed; if the retry then throws again (offline-erase.ts:374-376 only logs and keeps the marker), the account is left writing new content to a disk that still owes an erase, with the denial that was supposed to hold gone. The window before the retry also lets a durable client resume appends to entries the retry is about to delete.
searchedFor: Read OfflineRuntime effect ordering (rememberOfflineUser then retryPendingOfflineErase)

samples.summary: After standDown the chip's tooltip reports 'another-tab' although the cause was the SDK refusing the attach
samples.evidence: `giveUp` sets `stoodDown = subject`, which makes `decided` undefined (collab-document-provider.tsx:301-304). The `lapse` expression (321-328) then falls through `!permitted` and `!offlineEnabled` — both false on the path that could ever reach a stand-down — to the literal `"another-tab"`. The design requires the tooltip to name which case applies; here it names a cause ("This document is open in another tab, and that tab is the one saving it to this device") that is not the one that fired, since the app election was won and it was the SDK's own lock that refused.
searchedFor: Read the lapse ternary in collab-document-provider.tsx

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as the finding describes. `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` (offline-erase.ts:310-330) takes no identity and resolves `who = offlineUserId()`, which falls back to the localStorage mirror `wafflebase-offline-user` (offline-erase.ts:62,98-107). It then calls `denyOfflineWrites(who)` and `eraseOfflineData(store, who)` -> `store.dropAllForUser(who)` + `forgetDeviceSecret(who)` (offline-erase.ts:27-40; wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1133-1138), deleting that account's live entries (which carry the un-pushed change log) and archives. Grep confirms the mirror is written in exactly one production site, `rememberOfflineUser(userId)` inside OfflineRuntime's effect (offline-runtime.tsx:66); the only other production calls are the `undefined` spend calls inside offline-erase.ts itself (313,337). OfflineRuntime mounts only when `offlineInPlay = supportsClientKey() || getOfflinePersistenceEnabled(me.id)` (PrivateRoute.tsx:28-30,58); `supportsClientKey()` is a build-time pin check (yorkie-capabilities.ts:76-82, current pin 0.7.22 < MinClientKeyVersion 0.7.23) and the preference defaults to false (offline-persistence-preference.ts:28,103-110), so an account that never opted in on a rolled-back build never refreshes the mirror. The logout caller passes no identity either (api/auth.ts:134-136), and I found no guard anywhere comparing the mirrored id to the account signing out. The same stale id reaches purgeOfflineDocuments (offline-erase.ts:412, called at api/documents.ts:167,215 and api/workspaces.ts:136,167) and isOfflineUser (offline-erase.ts:116-118, api/workspaces.ts:159). Reach is narrower than unconditional — it requires the pin-rollback state the PrivateRoute.tsx:52-54 comment explicitly anticipates — but that is a reachability caveat, not a refutation ground; the missing identity check is real and its cost when it fires is cross-account data loss of un-pushed work.

finding.summary: The recovery offer toast (`duration: Infinity`, no close button) is never dismissed after a successful recovery; clicking its action a second time reports a false error
finding.evidence: `toast.warning('Some changes could not be saved', { id: `offline-recovery-${item.id}`, duration: Infinity, … })` at offline-runtime.tsx:324. `<Toaster />` is mounted with defaults (App.tsx:193) — no `closeButton` — which the chip's own comment confirms ("the warning is `duration: Infinity` with no close button", sync-status-chip.tsx:287). Nothing ever calls `toast.dismiss('offline-recovery-…')`: the success arm at line 350 raises a *new* toast with a different id and the unmount cleanup (line 223) only sets `cancelled`, stops the watcher and closes the store. So after `recoverOfflineCopy` succeeds and `store.dropArchive(work.id)` runs (offline-copy-recovery.ts:306), the original warning stays on screen permanently with its "Save a copy" action live. A second click re-enters `recoverOfflineCopy`, `rehydrateArchive` finds no archive and returns `undefined`, so `refused: 'unreadable'` fires `toast.error('Could not recover those changes', { description: 'The stored copy could not be read.' })` — an error about work that was recovered correctly moments earlier. Contrast the chip, which deliberately retracts its own infinite toast (sync-status-chip.tsx:265, 292-297).

verdict.reason: The finding claims "Nothing ever calls toast.dismiss('offline-recovery-…')" and that a second click on the infinite offer toast re-enters recoverOfflineCopy to produce a false 'unreadable' error. The code contradicts this on both counts. offline-runtime.tsx:326 binds the offer id to a local `offerId`, and the success arm at offline-runtime.tsx:378 calls `toast.dismiss(offerId)` immediately before raising the success toast at line 379 — retracting the exact toast that was raised at line 333/334 with the same id, so it cannot remain on screen with a live action after a successful recovery. Independently, offline-runtime.tsx:331 declares `let recovering = false` and the action handler at lines 349-352 returns early when `recovering` is true, blocking re-entry while a recovery is in flight; `recovering` is reset to false only on the refusal arm (line 362) and the rejection arm (line 399), i.e. only where nothing was consumed and the offer should legitimately stand. The reviewer's cited line numbers also do not match the file (the toast.warning is at line 333, not 324). offline-runtime.test.tsx:542 asserts `toastDismiss` was called with 'offline-recovery-1', confirming the retraction is exercised behaviour. A repo-wide grep for `toast.dismiss` / `recovering` shows only this one offer site, so there is no alternative un-dismissing path.
